claim: Recovery cannot safely identify a namespace snapshot base from LIST when covered logs may have been deleted; it needs a point-readable authority containing at least the namespace incarnation, authoritative checkpoint ID, and last epoch seal.
After any ambiguous send, a later definite rejection does not prove a ref ID is reusable because the earlier request can still land and occupy the key.
A ref ID may be reused only when no request was sent or every sent attempt has conclusive non-application proof; NoAttemptSent and pre-PUT local encode/apply failures are safe cases.
A random namespace incarnation must qualify ref logs, snapshots, manifests, files, fold cursors, and cleanup state so namespace rebirth cannot reuse old physical identities.
REBUILD can condemn a blob belonging to a live unowned manifest when manifest LIST omits that manifest but physical blob LIST includes the blob.
maybeSweepStalePrecommits does not reclaim current-epoch manifest bodies, so repeatedly staging manifests and destroying builds without abandon can leak without bound during a long-lived mount.
Catalog lifecycle needs durable reconciliation for interrupted Creating, Live, and Removing transitions, including an actor that idempotently completes each transition.
Catalog admission must reserve each entry's worst-case Removing and fold-seal representation so capacity can never refuse the transition needed to remove an admitted entry.

A dedicated slot-occupy primitive should return Created, Occupied(GetResult), or Unresolved, preserve occupant bytes and token, decode an occupied RefLogTxn or EpochSeal, and terminate immediately when it adopts a seal.
The first recovery or touch after every writer-epoch transition, including a clean transition, must CAS-walk and seal the previous nonempty stream; an adopted EpochSeal terminates the walk.
Every manifest named by an unconsumed removal record must be retained until the fold cursor passes that removal record, unless the blob-edge decrement is persisted independently of the manifest body.

GC verification must retain a strict grouped enumeration of all key classes and add negative controls for ambiguous-send reuse, hidden checkpoints, rebirth cleanup omissions, asymmetric REBUILD omissions, and current-epoch manifest growth.

The existing life_epoch allocator is server-root-wide rather than namespace-local, so changing it for one warm rebirth would leave the mount lease on the old epoch while changing it for a full remount would affect every namespace.
The rebirth protocol should mint an explicit catalog incarnation and qualify ref keys, verbatim keys, _ckpt, fold cursors, cleanup work, and cached namespace handles with it.
Deleting a snapshot candidate before its _ckpt pointer CAS can leave _ckpt pointing to a missing object because backend CAS checks the expected pointer token but not target existence.
Every snapshot newer than the current _ckpt must remain pinned while its publisher may still be live, including after the publisher has acknowledged the snapshot PUT but before pointer publication.
Concurrent _ckpt publishers must use a read/decode/merge/CAS loop that takes the semantic maximum of pointer fields and preserves unrelated fields.
If recovery reads a missing checkpoint base, it must reread _ckpt and restart when the authority token advanced; an unchanged authority with a missing base is corruption.
Namespace removal must exact-delete _ckpt while the catalog entry is Removing, then CAS-delete the catalog entry last.
Only the owning mounted writer or a successor that has claimed and fenced the server root may append an interrupted terminal removal record; ordinary GC must not append it.

Recovery must capture the mount fence generation at admission and require the same generation plus a non-superseded runtime for every slot-occupy, _ckpt CAS, and final install; remount must cancel or wait for recovery before rearming.
Every unsettled writer cleanup duty must be persisted before the build is retired, with a defined adopter, exact-delete completion, and retirement transaction.

Removal-tail protection scans must share the common round budget, cache decoded protection across candidates in a namespace, and retain every affected candidate when the authoritative frontier is not reached.
When an ambiguous ref append's exact GET remains absent, the current wedge can remain Unresolved forever and keep the namespace unavailable until an externally induced remount.
An absent-key wedge should retry conditional creation of the same (key, bytes) under the original fence generation, or use an explicitly automated epoch-close/remount escalation.
Creating reconciliation must bind the entry to creator mount identity or fence generation, wait for that authority to become terminal, and CAS-delete only an unchanged catalog token.
Catalog admission must reject creation unless the encoded catalog plus worst-case fold cursor and removal reservations fit within both the catalog cap and the 256 MiB fold-seal cap.

Normal orphan-manifest sweep cannot reclaim blobs from a deleted manifest when it emits no blob deltas, because those blobs never transition to zero in-degree and later condemn-nothing REBUILD preserves the leak.

An EpochSeal transaction must contain exactly one seal operation, no manifest edges or lifecycle changes, and prev_epoch_seal exactly on sequence 1 of every non-genesis epoch, including a sequence-1 seal.
Strict ref-key parsing that accepts only _log, _snap, and _cleanup will abort a fold round when _ckpt appears under cas/refs/<ns>/.

The _cleanup removal order must be changed only after incarnation-qualified catalog/key APIs and the PartWriteTxn rebirth gate are landed, and _ckpt must receive a singleton strict-key classification or a separately excluded prefix.
Probe A requires deterministic sampling cadence and durable sample due, performed, and skipped observability; its result must not be treated as a substitute for the mount-time store-quality gate.
Creation costs at least three conditional writes: catalog Creating, _ckpt creation, and catalog Live; _ckpt merge conflicts can require multiple GET/CAS attempts.
The v7 fold algorithm can delete a blob when namespace A has an acknowledged +1 at its next exact slot but LIST hides all of A's new keys and the fold carries A's old cursor without probing it.
Every destructive round must exact-GET cursor+1 for every Live or Removing catalog entry and suppress all destructive work if the common budget expires before every namespace has a frontier proof.

A hold recorded only as cursor C can be forgotten on a later round without a hint, allowing a visible -1 in another namespace to delete a blob protected by an unaccounted acknowledged +1 behind the hold.

A carried hold must persist {Held, reason-code, retry/backoff state} per (namespace, incarnation), force an exact retry without a hint, and suppress pool-wide destruction until a successful frontier walk or explicit operator repair clears it.
Deleting orphan manifest M before its blob nominations are adopted can leave M undiscoverable and its blobs without in-degree rows permanently.

Orphan-manifest nomination must exact-GET and decode M, submit neutral current-count touches without B2 or unmatched-removal accounting, adopt them through the fold seal/gc/state CAS, and exact-delete M only afterward.

Every namespace-scoped CAS operation should use a typed NamespaceHandle{namespace, incarnation, local_life_generation} through Pool, CasPlainObjects, PartWriteTxn, ref recovery/publishing, cleanup, and upper metadata operations.

Incarnation-qualified physical keys alone do not make a hot-reader catalog mismatch rejection guarantee true because a reader without a catalog read, local fence transition, or bounded refresh cannot observe a remote replacement.

Catalog admission must enforce the additive reservation predicate fold_fixed + Σ reserve_cursor(entry) + Σ reserve_removing_cleanup(entry) + Σ reserve_hold(entry) <= fold_seal_cap in addition to encoded_catalog(post).size <= catalog_cap.

A decommissioned server-root slot must not retire while any catalog entry owned by that root remains, and a claimed successor must enumerate catalog entries exactly and resume Removing entries without a terminal record.

Existing pre-release or soak pools require a quiesced format bump and recreation; startup against the old format must fail closed with a message naming pool recreation, while any preservation requires a separate offline migration protocol.

A ref-append wedge must retain the admitted fence generation and allow each foreground lane flush at most one bounded controller operation with that generation; unresolved outcomes retain the wedge for a later caller or remount.
A valid successor EpochSeal occupying a ref slot is conclusive rejection of the old transaction, not corruption.

If merging proposed _ckpt fields produces the exact current body, the publisher must return without a same-bytes CAS; recovery or merge retries must use the existing recovery deadline and bounded-restart accounting.
The strict ref-key grammar must parse <ns>/<incarnation>/{_log,_snap,_ckpt} canonically from right to left and explicitly refuse legacy keys.
Forced REBUILD can discard a durable classification-4 hold and later certify the broken namespace as quiet, allowing a visible B:-1 to delete a blob still named by A:C+2.

A forced REBUILD with a readable prior seal must carry every hold verbatim into the new baseline; a missing or undecodable prior hold authority must cause a pool-wide destructive hold or refusal, never an ordinary deletion-capable baseline.
A successful frontier walk clears a hold only when folding through the offending position and adopting that result in gc/state; reaching another absent expected-next does not clear it.
A higher witness that disappears above a held cursor is corruption, not evidence that the hold can be cleared.

The destructive-frontier proof must cover a delayed +1 after probing during condemnation, graduation, and exact deletion; Condemned metadata requires rematerialization and an old exact-token delete cannot remove the new incarnation.
A Creating catalog entry must categorically forbid publication, while a Removing entry must forbid new positive ownership and remain cataloged until terminal folding and cleanup.

The read-side guarantee for a stale namespace handle is stale old-incarnation bytes or NotFound, not guaranteed rejection; destructive cleanup must revalidate life and fence immediately before each delete.

Decommission must recover and append the missing terminal under its claimed fence when _ckpt is present, and when _ckpt is absent it must exact-CAS-remove the catalog entry or fail as corruption if finalization ordering cannot be established.
Classification 4 requires bounded hold fields and forbids those fields for other classifications; unknown, duplicate, or invalid field combinations must be rejected.
Every fold-seal PUT must verify encodeFoldSeal(...).size() <= fold_seal_cap, with the reservation estimator accounting for JSON escaping and framing.

After process termination following nomination adoption, no durable manifest-delete debt is specified, so an incomplete LIST can omit the manifest forever; this causes a manifest leak rather than blob data loss.

The verification model must include one shared blob and pool-wide in-degree and retirement state, with controls for late +1, catalog transitions, forced REBUILD after a hold, classification-4 codec limits, stale reads, duplicate nomination, token ABA, and _ckpt-absent decommission finalization.

A permanent ref-append wedge is demand-driven: without a later caller it performs no retry, and an independently occurring remount is only one possible escape; the unresolved operation was not acknowledged.
A format-generation migration must bump both the writer generation and backward floor, update version goldens, and require quiesced recreation so an old writer cannot touch the reused prefix.
A pool-wide-held baseline for a missing or undecodable prior fold seal is not representable by per-namespace ShardCoverage and has no defined operator-clear authority.

REBUILD must refuse when its prior fold seal is missing or undecodable, naming pool recreation as the recovery path, unless a separate authoritative non-auto-clearable pool hold and operator repair transition is defined.

Source-backed or tokened adoption rematerializes a condemned blob, while a tokenless adoptEvidence relink relies on a committed source edge and durably establishes the target edge before source removal.
Every ref-layer reader must hold a typed RefNamespaceId{namespace, incarnation} and return stale data or NotFound, never data from a reborn namespace; namespace-only ref helpers must be removed.

Classification-4 wire fields require exact bounded names and values, duplicate-field rejection, and a byte-exact worst-case reservation including escaped namespace text, framing, newline, and trailer growth.

Verification must force missing prior seals, disappearing held witnesses, an incarnation-dropping key builder, and an old-generation wedge result after successor seal adoption; recovery and wedge installs need a generation recheck under the install lock.
The catalog size bound is O(Live + Creating + Removing), and removal costs at least a Live→Removing CAS, terminal append, exact _ckpt deletion, and catalog-removal CAS.

The selected CAS ref design uses one exact-readable pool catalog, one fixed mutable head per namespace, immutable predecessor-linked transaction nodes, and a head CAS as the transaction commit point; LIST discovers garbage candidates only.
The previous design treated ref IDs as sparse because next_ref_sequence was pool-wide, rejected writes burned safe gaps, and replay validated strict increase rather than contiguity.

The previous design treated immutable log PUT as durability even though semantic application depended on later in-memory installation, creating possibly durable-but-not-applied state after an ambiguous PUT.
A ref transaction is committed if and only if it is reachable from the namespace's exact-read _head.
An immutable node that landed but was never installed into _head is inert garbage with no owner semantics and is never folded.
The ref-node sequence is dense and per-incarnation, with node.sequence = parent.sequence + 1; failed candidate nodes do not create committed-chain gaps.

The namespace head must update monotonically: transaction updates point to a node whose previous is the old tip, checkpoint updates preserve the tip and advance coverage only, and recovery fences preserve tip/checkpoint while changing writer_epoch.

The chosen key layout uses cas/ref_catalog, cas/refs/<ns>/_head, cas/refs/<ns>/<incarnation>/_node/<sequence16>-<sha256-of-canonical-node>.zst, cas/refs/<ns>/<incarnation>/_snapshot/<covered-sequence16>-<sha256-of-canonical-snapshot>.zst, cas/manifests/<ns>/<incarnation>/<build-id>/..., and roots/<ns>/<incarnation>/....
A missing or undecodable ref_catalog after the pool format exists is corruption, and all mutations and destructive work must stop rather than reconstruct it from LIST.
ref_catalog is a sorted map from logical namespace to random 128-bit incarnation and contains active namespaces plus namespaces waiting for terminal removal to fold, without permanent tombstones.

Namespace creation chooses a random incarnation, creates or CAS-replaces _head with an empty head, CAS-adds {namespace, incarnation} to ref_catalog, and waits for an exact catalog read-back before the first owner transaction commits.

The immutable node PUT is not the commit point: a writer conditionally creates the node, token-CASes _head to the new tip, and acknowledges only after the exact head shows the proposed tip and local installation is complete.
If local installation throws after _head commits, the lane closes and recovers from _head; an ambiguous head CAS closes the namespace and invokes recovery-fence handling.

Recovery exact-reads ref_catalog, _head, and the checkpoint named by _head, follows exact node links while verifying namespace, incarnation, body hash, dense sequence, and acyclicity, then CAS-fences _head with the new writer_epoch before installing state.
If an old append CAS commits before recovery fencing, recovery rereads and adopts the node; if the fence commits first, the old CAS is permanently invalid because its expected token is stale.

GC exact-reads ref_catalog and every namespace _head, follows each sampled tip back to its exact cursor, and suppresses all destructive work when the cursor is not an ancestor or a node is missing, malformed, or over budget.
A safe GC cursor equals a sampled authoritative head, and every node on the unique path from the old cursor to that head has been exact-read and folded.

Snapshot cleanup may delete a listed node or snapshot only when point-readable facts prove the GC cursor covers it, the current head checkpoint covers it, and it is neither the current tip nor current checkpoint.

The orphan-manifest sweep protects every current committed or precommit manifest and every removed manifest named by exact chain nodes above the GC cursor, and deletes only a listed eligible manifest with its exact current token.
A current-epoch build prefix is eligible for orphan cleanup only after its build duty is conclusively settled; PartWriteTxn must not retire a build while an ownership-granting head CAS is ambiguous.

Namespace removal commits one terminal node containing every owner -1 and RemoveNamespace, forbids later operations in that incarnation, folds that terminal head, cleans incarnation-qualified manifests/files, and CAS-removes the catalog entry.
Physical emptiness is not a rebirth precondition because old objects are incarnation-qualified; omitted old objects are retained rather than guessed dead after the catalog entry is removed.

REBUILD exact-reads the catalog and every head at a sampled tip, emits baseline +1 edges for current owners, sets baseline cursors to sampled tips, refuses missing committed manifests or broken chains, and publishes with destructive work suppressed.
A physical blob LIST during REBUILD may nominate zero-edge blobs for condemnation, but omitted blobs remain leaked and are not treated as proof of absence.

fsck must use exact catalog and head state for logical integrity, retry a namespace if its head changes, and report missing catalog/head/node/checkpoint state as non-clean and unchecked rather than as an empty namespace.
Physical LIST results in fsck are only observed garbage candidates; fsck must not claim that no unaccounted physical objects exist.

The catalog is a high-value control object with an encoded-size limit; admission must fail before the limit, and the bound applies to concurrently active or removing namespaces rather than lifetime churn.
The CAS ref design relies on exact-GET and token-CAS backend semantics; a backend that violates those primitives is outside the admissible pool contract and must fail its capability probe.

Since TXN-ONE-PIPELINE Task 1.1, B151 CA durable publish operations ran inside MergeTreeData::Transaction::commit while holding the data_parts lock, causing concurrent queries needing that lock to stall behind S3 round trips.

The soak harness missed the lock-stall defect because it measured memory and correctness rather than query latency, and its all-INSERT/OPTIMIZE workload did not queue independent readers on the parts lock.
ProfileEvents::PartsLockHoldMicroseconds and ProfileEvents::PartsLockWaitMicroseconds already instrument parts-lock hold and wait time, and DataPartsLock carries wait_watch and lock_watch.
The soak phase-3 ticker should sample per-tick deltas of PartsLockHoldMicroseconds, PartsLockWaitMicroseconds, and ContextLockWaitMicroseconds, then gate runs on a calibrated per-tick hold budget.
A latency canary should issue a cheap point SELECT and a small system.parts scan about every 100 ms, recording latency and failing when canary p99 outside chaos windows exceeds the threshold.

A debug guard should track whether the current thread holds DataPartsLock or DataPartsSharedLock and assert at synchronous CA or S3 network primitives that network I/O is not occurring under a hot parts lock.
Audit every public operation in ContentAddressedMetadataStorage, ContentAddressedTransaction, and object-storage entry points by latency class, S3 round trips, state dependence, and lock context.
Audit every mutex, SharedMutex, and condition variable in the CA tree for protected state, longest critical-section operation, waiters, cutoff or indefinite-wedge behavior, and fencing interaction.
The monitoring guide should alert on the server-wide per-table rate of PartsLockHoldMicroseconds and PartsLockWaitMicroseconds after enabling metric_log in the nightly image.
Post-soak validation should mine system.query_log ProfileEvents for PartsLockWaitMicroseconds, S3 request counters, and Keeper wait events to identify SELECT outliers.

The current CAS integration maps untyped disk-relative strings through PartPathParser and routing code to reconstruct table, part, projection, detached/shadow, and in-part file identity before reaching typed CAS objects.
Path reconstruction is fragile because the abstraction boundary erases the MergeTree object structure, requiring independently evolving path grammars to continue agreeing.
The path parser must recognize Atomic and non-Atomic layouts, temporary part prefixes, detached, projections, FREEZE shadow paths, table-level files, and generic mountpoint files.
A non-Atomic table named detached cannot always be distinguished from the reserved detached-parts directory when only the path string remains.
IDataPartStorage provides part-relative operations including existsFile, prepareRead, writeFile, createHardLinkFrom, rename, projection creation, cloning, removal, and transaction lifecycle.

CAS should keep the logical part format Full; it changes physical representation and publication protocol, not the independent MergeTree files such as checksums.txt, columns, marks, projections, and metadata.
A candidate DataPartStorageContentAddressed would carry typed CAS root namespace, ref, and optional projection-relative prefix, while file operations add only the part-relative file name.

The inheritance of DataPartStorageContentAddressed is unresolved among overriding DataPartStorageOnDiskBase, extracting reusable mechanics, implementing IDataPartStorage directly, or incrementally wrapping Full behavior.
A typed CAS part-storage implementation can preserve table namespace, part ref, projection prefix, and relative file name as separate values from construction through publication.
A dedicated CAS part-storage implementation could own in-flight read, size, existence, and directory-listing overlays so ordinary DataPartStorageOnDiskFull retains ordinary disk semantics.

A dedicated part storage cannot remove the generic path router because startup discovery, detached and shadow enumeration, table-level files, loose mountpoint objects, diagnostics, and direct IDisk clients still require a filesystem view.
IDataPartStorage::precommitTransaction is called before final part rename and therefore is not automatically a safe externally visible CAS publication boundary.
The public ClickHouse tree has no table-level durable part-registry interface such as IPartRegistry, IDataPartsStorage, or IPartCatalog.
CAS table refs represent the filesystem-like physical inventory, not the richer MergeTreeData active-parts registry or Keeper's expected per-replica part set.
DataPartStorageContentAddressed addresses only part identity -> manifest entries and files; it does not replace table identity -> durable set of physical parts.

A future IDataPartStorageRoot would be a substantially larger upstream redesign touching startup discovery, reconciliation, storage-policy disks, detached/shadow enumeration, and replicated expected-part logic, and is not implied by the current concern.

A new CA part-storage implementation requires a centralized factory because direct construction in fetch, part loading, and temporary text-index code could otherwise create two part-storage semantics on one disk.

Cross-storage operations must define same-CAS manifest adoption, CA-to-ordinary copy, ordinary-to-CA copy, and movement between different CAS pools without concrete-type assumptions in fetch, clone, mutation, or storage-policy moves.
During migration, typed and generic path operations must resolve to exactly the same namespace, ref, and manifest entry, with equivalence tests for the two access paths.

Before TXN-ONE-PIPELINE becomes an implementation plan, a spike must determine whether a part-storage boundary removes enough shared patches and routing complexity to justify its larger implementation.

The proposed spike should centralize DataPartStorageOnDiskFull construction, add a skeletal DataPartStorageContentAddressed for CA disks, implement one typed committed read and transactional write, test temporary-to-final rename and projection transaction sharing, and compare typed and path-derived routes.
Until the design questions are answered, DataPartStorageContentAddressed remains an architectural alternative rather than an implementation commitment.
D10 requires a code change because TEST(CasRefCatalogAdmission, Predicate2AcceptsEqualityRefusesOneEntryOver) names an entry-count boundary rather than byte equality.
D21 contains runtime report.recordAnomaly strings in CasGc.cpp, so removing its branch-local Task 5 references requires code review rather than a prose-only edit.

D23 has a timing conflict: narrowing CasPool.h to namespace-file reads would become an understatement after code removes catalog admission from listRefs, resolveRef, and dropNamespace; the code and prose changes must be sequenced together.
CasPool.cpp line 1412's statement that a function has four callers is stale because the classification lists at least six non-test call sites.
The policy requires removing branch-local review provenance from code comments, including counts corrected by review rounds, plan commit hashes, stage/directive citations, and BACKLOG citations.
